q.t: The coloured patches on spoiled food are…
q.e: Mould is alive — thousands of tiny microbes.

q.t: Microbes are…
o: Living things too small to see without a microscope
q.e: They are tiny living things found almost everywhere.

q.t: Turning milk into curd is the work of…
q.e: Helpful microbes ferment milk into curd.

q.t: Drying chillies in the sun preserves them by removing…
q.e: Microbes need water to grow; dry food stays safe.

q.t: Which teeth cut and bite food?
q.e: Incisors are flat, sharp-edged and at the front.

q.t: Which teeth grind food?
q.e: Large, flat molars at the back grind food.

q.t: Which teeth tear food?
q.e: Pointed canines tear food.

q.t: A cavity is…
q.e: Acid made by microbes dissolves the tooth surface, forming a hole.

q.t: A fridge keeps food fresh by…
q.e: Cold slows microbes down but does not kill them.

q.t: Idli batter rises overnight because of…
q.e: Microbes feed on the batter and release gas that gets trapped.

q.t: Why does oil on top of a pickle keep it from spoiling?
o: It keeps air away from the food
q.e: The oil layer is a seal — most spoilage microbes need air.

q.t: Why does ghee keep for months but butter spoils quickly?
o: Ghee has had its water boiled off
q.e: No water means no microbes.

q.t: Salting fish preserves it because salt…
q.e: Without moisture, microbes can't grow.

q.t: Jam lasts long because of…
o: Lots of sugar removing available moisture
q.e: Sugaring, like salting, takes away the moisture microbes need.

q.t: Why do cavities form?
o: Microbes turn leftover sugar into acid
q.e: Acid from microbes slowly dissolves the tooth surface.

q.t: Why are cutting teeth at the front?
o: Food arrives there and must be bitten off
q.e: A thin sharp edge at the front bites off food as it enters.

q.t: Why are grinding teeth at the back?
o: The bite is strongest near the jaw hinge
q.e: Like a nutcracker: closer to the pivot, greater force.

q.t: A matka keeps water cool because…
o: Water seeping out evaporates and takes away heat
q.e: Evaporation from the pot's surface cools the water inside.

q.t: Why not talk or laugh with food in your mouth?
o: Food can go into the air passage and cause choking
q.e: Food and air share a passage; laughing opens the air route at the wrong time.

q.t: Curd helps an upset stomach because its microbes…
o: Support the helpful microbes in the gut
q.e: Its microbes reinforce the useful ones already in the gut.

q.t: Every preservation method works by…
q.e: Once you know what microbes need — moisture, air, warmth — you can work out any method.

q.t: Why does bread spoil in two days but pickle lasts two months?
o: Bread is moist and exposed; pickle is sealed with oil and salt
q.e: The pickle denies microbes air and moisture; bread gives them both.

q.t: Frozen food keeps longer than refrigerated food because…
o: Freezing locks the water so microbes can't use it
q.e: Microbes can't use frozen water, but they're still alive — thawed food spoils fast.

q.t: A piece of mango sticks out above the oil in a pickle jar. What may happen?
o: It spoils and can spoil the rest
q.e: Without the oil seal, air reaches it and microbes grow.

q.t: Idli batter left in a cold room doesn't rise. Why?
o: Microbes slow down in the cold
There's no air in cold rooms
q.e: The same reason a fridge preserves food: cold slows microbes.

q.t: Which is more harmful for teeth?
o: A sweet sucked slowly all afternoon
A sweet eaten quickly and rinsed
q.e: The danger is how long sugar stays on the teeth.

q.t: Why does a far-travelled mango often taste less good?
o: It was picked before it was ripe
q.e: Fruit that travels for days must be picked unripe to survive the journey.

q.t: Fermentation and spoilage are both microbes breaking down food. The difference is…
q.e: We call it fermentation when we want it, spoilage when we don't.

q.t: Chewing food properly helps digestion because it…
o: Makes small pieces and releases saliva
q.e: Small pieces give more surface for juices, and saliva starts digestion.

q.t: Spices like pepper and turmeric help preserve food by…
q.e: They slow microbe growth.

q.t: A new method blows hot, dry air over fruit slices. Will it preserve them? Why?
q.e: Drying removes the water microbes need — you can predict this from the rule.

q.t: Why is canned food safe for a long time?
o: It is airtight and keeps new microbes out
q.e: Canning removes air and seals out new microbes.

q.t: By the time you can see mould, spoilage is…
q.e: One microbe is invisible; you see the colony only after thousands have grown.

q.t: The tongue's job while eating is to…
o: Pass food back from cutting to grinding teeth
q.e: It moves food from incisors to canines to premolars to molars.

q.t: Why does brushing prevent cavities?
o: It removes food before microbes make acid
q.e: No leftover sugar means microbes can't make acid.

q.t: Hunting wasps store paralysed prey for their larvae. This is an example of…
q.e: Hunting wasps preserved food long before humans did.

q.t: Vasco da Gama crossed oceans to reach India partly for…
q.e: Black pepper was hugely valuable, partly because it helped preserve food.

q.t: Taking food out of the fridge and leaving it warm…
q.e: Cold only slowed them; warmth wakes them up.

q.t: Which pair is matched correctly?
q.e: Oil seals out air. Drying and salting remove moisture; refrigeration lowers temperature.

q.t: Gulping food without chewing can cause indigestion because…
o: The stomach gets work that should have been half done
q.e: Without chewing and saliva, digestion starts late and is less complete.
